title: Stop the Scroll in 3 Seconds
subtitle: How 50 fill-in-the-blank hooks turn strangers into viewers
intro: You have 3 seconds before someone scrolls past you. Your saved post promises 50 lines that can freeze that thumb.
takeaway: A good hook earns 3 seconds of attention so your story can earn the next 30.

sections.heading: Everyday analogy: the shop window
sections.body:
Think of your video like a shop on a busy street. A hook is the window display that makes you stop walking.

You don't see the whole store yet, just one surprising sign. That sign decides if you walk in.

Your Instagram feed is that street, and the hook is your sign — so let's see why you need one.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? Attention you can't waste
sections.body:
Attention-grabbing hook means the first line that stops scrolling. Storytelling template means a fill-in-the-blank sentence you reuse.

Your save gives you 10 examples like: "I wasted (insert time period) doing (insert habit)..." You just add your story.

That works because people decide in 3 seconds if they'll stay. A ready template saves you from guessing every time — but copy-paste alone can backfire, which is next.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? When hooks flop
sections.body:
If your hook promises drama but your story is flat, viewers feel tricked and leave.

If you use the same hook as everyone else — like "Nobody talks about this phase..." — you blend in instead of standing out.

Fix it by matching the hook to a real moment from your life, then delivering the payoff fast.

steps.narration: You are scrolling fast past dozens of posts.
A hook like 'I did everything right and still failed' makes you pause.
The next lines must deliver the real story you promised.
If it delivers, you engage instead of scrolling.
If it doesn't match, you leave and trust drops.

quiz.q: What is a storytelling hook in plain words?
options: The hashtags at the end of a post
The first line that makes you stop scrolling
The filter you use on video
The time you post each day
quiz.why: A hook's job is to earn the first 3 seconds of attention so the rest can be watched.

quiz.q: What can go wrong if you copy a fill-in-the-blank hook exactly?
options: You will get more views no matter what
Viewers may feel tricked or bored if it doesn't fit your story
quiz.why: The save gives templates, but if the hook doesn't match your real story, people scroll away.

quiz.q: What fails first if you use the same viral hook as everyone else?
options: You blend in and get ignored
You get banned from using templates
quiz.why: When thousands use 'Nobody talks about this...' it stops feeling surprising.

extra: Test hooks by writing 3 versions of the same story and seeing which keeps viewers past the 3-second mark.

judge.why: D2 is the most beginner-friendly and concise, defines key terms in plain words, uses one clear shop-window analogy with good flow, grounds its examples in the saved hooks, and clearly marks its testing tip as extra; its quiz checks understanding rather than recall.
